title: Creamy Chicken & Bacon Penne
subtitle: penne with golden chicken, crisp bacon and sweet peas in a garlic Parmesan cream sauce
imageAlt: Creamy penne with chicken pieces, bacon bits and green peas in a white bowl on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Save a cup of pasta water before draining; it makes the sauce silky.

steps.title: Water on
steps.text: Bring a big pot of water to a boil with the salt.

steps.title: Bacon
steps.text: Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium, 6–8 minutes, until crisp. Lift it onto paper towel and pour off all but 1 tbsp fat.

steps.title: Chicken
steps.text: Toss the chicken with the garlic powder, salt and pepper. Cook it in the bacon fat over medium-high, 6–7 minutes, stirring now and then, until golden and 74°C (165°F). Move to a plate.

steps.title: Pasta
steps.text: Cook the penne 1 minute less than the package says, adding the peas for the last minute. Scoop out 1 cup of the water, then drain.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Lower the skillet to medium-low. Cook the garlic 30 seconds, add the cream and broth and simmer 2–3 minutes, scraping up the brown bits. Stir in the Parmesan until smooth.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Add the pasta, peas, chicken and half the bacon and toss, adding pasta water a splash at a time until glossy. Top with the rest of the bacon.

fixIt.fix: Loosen with the saved pasta water; it thickens as it sits.
The heat was too high when the Parmesan went in. Keep it at medium-low and stir it in off the boil.
Cut evenly and pull it at 74°C (165°F); it warms again in the sauce.

saleTip: No Frills bacon is often 2 for $10; freeze it in 6-slice packs.
swap: Half-and-half instead of cream: lighter, and the Parmesan still thickens it; don't let it boil hard.
leftovers: Add a splash of milk or broth when reheating; the sauce soaks into the pasta.
doneness: Chicken pieces at 74°C (165°F) (Health Canada, poultry pieces). Reheat to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested creamy chicken bacon pasta methods (Canadian Living, Delish): bacon rendered first, chicken cooked in the fat, a garlic cream and Parmesan pan sauce loosened with pasta water.
prepAhead: Cut the chicken and chop the bacon up to 1 day ahead.
Cook the bacon ahead; it re-crisps in the pan in 1 minute.
reheat: Covered in the microwave with a splash of milk, 2–3 minutes, stirring halfway, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Chicken, bacon and Parmesan cream; no peas.

fancy.note: Blistered cherry tomatoes and lemon zest to brighten it.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: after the bacon, blister the cherry tomatoes in the fat over high heat 3–4 minutes; set them aside with the bacon.

addSteps.title: Finish
addSteps.text: Fold in the blistered tomatoes and grate the lemon zest over each bowl.

why.1-0: Cooking the chicken in the bacon fat seasons it all the way through.
why.0-2: Frozen peas cook in the pasta water in 1 minute and add sweetness.
why.2-3: Parmesan both thickens and seasons the cream.

funFact: Penne is named for the quill pen, 'penna' in Italian; its angled ends were cut to look like a nib.
